title: An \textit{ab initio} based compact analytical formula for inelastic x-ray scattering from spatially localized excitons
authors: Joris Sturm, Duc Anh Truong, Andrei Benediktovitch, Nina Rohringer, Andreas Knorr$^{1}$
abstract: In this contribution we provide a compact model for the description of inelastic x-ray scattering of spatially localized excitons. We combine our analytical theory with first principles calculations and apply it to the material lithium fluoride (LiF). A comparison of two different approaches for the underlying single-particle wave functions to calculate the spectrum yield a qualitatively good agreement with experimental data but also shows that a detailed description of the wave functions is essential to obtain qualitative results.
summary: This work develops a compact analytical model to calculate the inelastic x-ray scattering spectrum arising from excitons in materials like LiF. By comparing theoretical approaches—specifically ab initio MLWF versus simpler LCAO methods—the authors demonstrate that the accuracy of the calculated spectrum critically depends on the detailed description of the underlying electronic wave functions. This provides a vital theoretical tool for interpreting high-resolution spectroscopic measurements of excitonic excitations.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide a compact analytical formula for describing inelastic x-ray scattering (IXS) from spatially localized excitons.
main_result: The derived formulas show that the choice of wave function description—specifically comparing tight-binding (LCAO) versus ab initio (MLWF) methods—is crucial, with MLWF yielding superior agreement with experimental data for the exciton spectrum.
method: The theoretical framework combines analytical theory with first-principles calculations (DFT/BSE) to model the scattering cross-section, comparing localized and extended exciton contributions.
model_or_system: The system studied is the insulator Lithium Fluoride (LiF), focusing on excitons (electron-hole pairs). The theory models the scattering spectrum $S(\Delta q, \omega)$ using excitonic basis sets derived from Bloch states and Wannier functions.
important_parameters:
Momentum transfer ($\Delta q$), energy loss ($\omega$), and the distinction between localized ($R_n=0$) and extended ($R_n 
eq 0$) exciton regimes.
main_assumptions:
The localized case assumes the contribution from non-vanishing lattice vectors ($R_n 
eq 0$) is a small perturbation, and both limiting cases only consider optically active $s$-like excitonic states.
figures_summary: The figures compare the predicted IXS spectra using LCAO vs. MLWF approaches, showing MLWF's better agreement with experimental data, especially at low momentum transfer.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by relating the spectrum to correlation functions, deriving separate formulas for localized and extended excitons, and then validates these formulas by applying them to LiF using both LCAO and ab initio (MLWF) calculations.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection between advanced many-body theory (BSE) and measurable spectroscopic techniques (IXS) provides a powerful tool for characterizing quasiparticle excitations in solids, which is relevant to understanding strongly correlated or excitonic physics.

Similar to Fig. 1 we show the experimental data (colored) in the background to provide a direct comparison to the theoretical results. It is evident, that by employing the MLWF approach, in contrast to the tight-binding approach (Fig. 1) we now also obtain spectral features at lower momentum transfer centered around ∆qx = 0.8.
